title: Coding Challenge 4: Polymorphism
description: Learn the principle of Polymorphism in Object-Oriented Programming. Polymorphism allows different classes to define methods with the same name, enabling code to interact with them through a shared interface while each responds in its own way. Create a Superhero base class and subclasses (FlyingHero and SpeedHero) that each implement usePower() differently, along with an activatePowers() function that triggers powers across a superhero team.
requirements: Create a base class named 'Superhero' with a constructor accepting 'name'
Implement a 'usePower()' method on Superhero returning '[name] uses a superpower!'
Create a 'FlyingHero' class that extends Superhero and overrides 'usePower()' to return '[name] flies through the skies!'
Create a 'SpeedHero' class that extends Superhero and overrides 'usePower()' to return '[name] runs at supersonic speed!'
Create an 'activatePowers(heroes)' function that takes an array of heroes, calls usePower() on each polymorphically, and returns an array of the results
hints: Use 'class FlyingHero extends Superhero' to inherit from Superhero
Subclasses inherit constructor(name) automatically if they don't declare their own constructor
Override a parent method simply by declaring usePower() in the subclass
Polymorphism means activatePowers works for any Superhero subtype without checking its specific class type

tests.name: Superhero base class exists with name property
tests.test: function() { try { const hero = new Superhero('Mystic'); return (typeof hero === 'object' && hero.name === 'Mystic') ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Superhero class missing or name property not set' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Superhero has usePower() method
tests.test: function() { try { const hero = new Superhero('Mystic'); const res = hero.usePower(); return res === 'Mystic uses a superpower!' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Mystic uses a superpower!", got "' + res + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: FlyingHero extends Superhero and overrides usePower()
tests.test: function() { try { const fly = new FlyingHero('Skyhawk'); if (!(fly instanceof Superhero)) { return { success: false, message: 'FlyingHero must extend Superhero' }; } const res = fly.usePower(); return res === 'Skyhawk flies through the skies!' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Skyhawk flies through the skies!", got "' + res + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: SpeedHero extends Superhero and overrides usePower()
tests.test: function() { try { const speed = new SpeedHero('Bolt'); if (!(speed instanceof Superhero)) { return { success: false, message: 'SpeedHero must extend Superhero' }; } const res = speed.usePower(); return res === 'Bolt runs at supersonic speed!' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Bolt runs at supersonic speed!", got "' + res + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: activatePowers() polymorphically executes usePower() across heroes
tests.test: function() { try { if (typeof activatePowers !== 'function') { return { success: false, message: 'activatePowers function does not exist' }; } const team = [new FlyingHero('Aero'), new SpeedHero('Flash'), new Superhero('Citizen')]; const results = activatePowers(team); const expected = ['Aero flies through the skies!', 'Flash runs at supersonic speed!', 'Citizen uses a superpower!']; if (!Array.isArray(results) || results.length !== 3) { return { success: false, message: 'activatePowers should return an array with 3 power messages' }; } const matches = results.every((msg, idx) => msg === expected[idx]); return matches ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected ' + JSON.stringify(expected) + ', got ' + JSON.stringify(results) }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Subclasses respond differently to the same interface
tests.test: function() { try { const h1 = new FlyingHero('Valkyrie'); const h2 = new SpeedHero('Velocity'); const team = [h1, h2]; const outputs = team.map(h => h.usePower()); return (outputs[0] === 'Valkyrie flies through the skies!' && outputs[1] === 'Velocity runs at supersonic speed!') ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Different subclasses failed to provide polymorphic responses' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
